vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skillup
Version: 0.1.5

The SkillUp bundle is a legitimate utility designed to automate the validation, packaging, and publishing of OpenClaw skills to platforms like GitHub, Xiaping (xiaping.coze.site), and ClawHub (clawhub.ai). The scripts (scripts/publish.sh and associated library files) use standard system tools such as curl, git, and the GitHub CLI (gh) to perform their stated functions. While the tool handles sensitive API tokens, it does so through standard environment variables and configuration files, directing them only to the intended service endpoints. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: SkillUp is coherent with its stated purpose (packaging and publishing skills to GitHub, Xiaping, OpenClaw, and ClawHub); the requested binaries and environment variables match that purpose and the runtime scripts implement the described flows.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim to package and publish skills to GitHub, Xiaping, OpenClaw, and ClawHub. Required binaries (git, gh, curl, claw, clawhub) and optional python3/zip are exactly what a cross-platform publisher would need. The required env vars map 1:1 to the four target platforms and the primary credential is the GitHub token — all proportionate to the declared functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included shell scripts direct the agent to discover skill directories, validate metadata, create zip artifacts, and upload/publish to the configured platforms (via CLI or HTTP). The scripts read skill files (SKILL.md, manifest.toml), a config file, and write logs and temporary files under /tmp and an artifact directory. They also set/ export tokens for CLI invocation and use curl to POST artifacts to remote endpoints. This behavior is expected for a publisher, but it does mean the skill will transmit packaged skill contents and use provided credentials to remote services.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec — the package is instruction-plus-scripts only. That is low risk compared to remote download/install steps. All code is present in the bundle and executed as shell scripts; nothing is fetched from arbitrary URLs during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests four platform-specific credentials (SKILLUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, SKILLUP_XIAPING_API_KEY, SKILLUP_OPENCLAW_TOKEN, SKILLUP_CLAWHUB_TOKEN) plus an alternate CLAWHUB_TOKEN. These map directly to the four publishing targets and are proportionate. Caveat: the scripts export tokens into environment for CLI calls and include Authorization headers in curl requests; command outputs and /tmp logs may inadvertently capture sensitive information depending on CLI behavior. Use least-privilege tokens and rotate them if used here.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request forced always-on presence or attempts to modify other skills' configuration. It executes as-needed and writes artifacts/logs to local artifact directories and /tmp only (expected for a publisher).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: packaging and publishing skills to the four named platforms. Before installing or running it: (1) Inspect the config.example.toml and set only the platforms you intend to use. (2) Provide least-privilege API tokens (e.g., scoped GitHub tokens limited to the target repo rather than full account access) and rotate them after use. (3) Run with --dry-run first to validate behavior without uploading. (4) Be aware the scripts write logs and temporary files under /tmp and may capture CLI output — avoid passing highly privileged tokens unless you trust the target endpoints. (5) If you plan to run this in an automated agent, review the included shell scripts (they are present in the bundle) and confirm the Xiaping and ClawHub base URLs match the real services you intend to publish to. If anything seems unexpected (unknown target URLs or a token you don't recognize), do not proceed and ask for clarification.
